issues: Whether ceasing to dispatch an owner-operator constitutes a dismissal or adverse action under Part II of the Canada Labour Code
Whether an employer's adverse action is an unfair labour practice where the employee's union activity was a factor in the decision, even if other reasons are also cited
The allocation of the burden of proof in an unfair labour practice proceeding and the prima facie case the complainant must establish
What an employer must demonstrate to establish a legitimate, non-discriminatory reason for an adverse action taken while a certification application is pending
The evidentiary significance of the temporal proximity between the employer's withdrawal of certification objections and the adverse action against the employee

The weight to be given to an employer's evidence that relies on unnamed informants, hearsay, and old disciplinary records where the employer fails to call witnesses with first-hand knowledge of the events relied upon

Whether an employer's stated reasons for an adverse action are credible where the employee provided a medical note and regularly contacted the dispatcher, and the employer's owner testified to having no knowledge of the employee's union involvement
key_facts: owner-operator hauling marine containers for a federally regulated trucking company
employee was the elected drivers' representative during an industry-wide port dispute
employee was active in the union that applied for certification of the employer's drivers
certification application was pending at the time of the adverse action
employer hired counsel to oppose certification and dropped objections shortly before the adverse action
employee was off work with a non-work-related sprained ankle and provided a medical note
employee called the dispatcher several times a week and was told work was slow
employee was told he would no longer be dispatched because someone had seen him working elsewhere
employer's owner was the sole witness at the hearing
employer relied on unnamed informants, old warning letters, and a list of missed Mondays
employer did not call the dispatcher or any person with first-hand knowledge
causes_of_action: unfair labour practice under s. 94(1)(b) of the Canada Labour Code (discrimination against an employee because of union membership or activity)
candidate_statutes: Canada Labour Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. L-2, Part II, s. 94
Canada Labour Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. L-2, Part II, s. 95
search_terms: prima facie case unfair labour practice
